title: Explosive plays: why one long catch flips a game (and how to spot the shot play in your drill)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run: it still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, last updated Oct 12) and no review files. The original football-film-room repository wasn't reachable (access denied: not configured for this session). So there's no new miss of yours to fix, and no snap of yours this connects to yet. This lesson comes from Thursday night: Green Bay trailed Carolina 10-6 until Christian Watson's 53-yard catch, and then scored 21 straight points.

The big idea: most drives move the ball 4 or 5 yards at a time. An explosive play skips that work. Analysts usually count a pass of 20+ yards or a run of 10+ yards as explosive (some use 12+ for runs). Drives with one end in points far more often, because the offense needs fewer chances to stay on schedule. One explosive play can matter more than ten good ones.

White = offense, yellow = defense. Solid white arrows are routes; the dashed white line is the throw. Yellow dashed arrows: the linebackers moving toward the fake. Numbers 1–4 match the steps below.

  1. 1. Fake the run. The quarterback pretends to hand off (play-action, Lesson 16).2. Linebackers are taught to stop the run, so they take a step forward. That step empties the middle of the field behind them.
  2. 3. Find the one deep safety. In a 1-high shell (Lesson 20), one safety guards the whole deep middle.4. Send two receivers deep on different sides of him. He can only go to one. The other is open, or covered only by a cornerback running with him.
  3. Thursday's example. Green Bay's short game was efficient (Love 23 of 25 on throws out in under 2.5 seconds, but only 177 yards).The points came from the longer throws: 7 of 14 for 154 yards and 2 TDs on throws of 10+ yards (Next Gen Stats via NFL.com). Watson's 53-yarder flipped a 10-6 deficit.
  4. Saturday's examples. Arizona's Noah Fifita hit Isaiah Mizell for a 94-yard TD at Texas Tech after a scramble.Rutgers' backup AJ Surace was 3 of 12 at Michigan, but one throw went 80 yards for a TD: two-thirds of his 123 yards.Runs count too: J'Koby Williams' 64-yard TD for Texas Tech, and Carson Hansen's 42-yard run for Penn State today.
  5. How defenses stop them. Two deep safeties (2-high) "keep the ball in front": they give up short throws and runs to take away the deep shot (Lesson 20).That's why a 2-high shell often means a long, slow drive, and a 1-high shell invites a shot.

How to log it in your drill: on 1st-and-10 or 2nd-and-short, a quarterback under center (or a back right beside him in the shotgun), wide receivers split out wide and one safety deep in the middle is the classic shot setup. Log it PASS, even though the first thing you see is a fake handoff. Two other times teams take shots: the first play after a turnover ("sudden change"), and right after a long run, when the linebackers are thinking run.

Why it matters for your bets: totals are built on drive-by-drive scoring. One or two explosive plays can push a low game over. Thursday's Under survived at 46 even with Watson's 53 yards. For Sunday's Chiefs-Broncos Under 40.5, the thing to watch is whether Denver keeps two safeties deep against Patrick Mahomes.

Real examples to watch (Pacific time): Sunday, Ravens at Bills (10:00 a.m., CBS): Lamar Jackson's play-action against Buffalo. Chiefs at Broncos (1:25 p.m., CBS): Mahomes against Denver's safeties. Tonight in college: Ohio State at USC (4:30 p.m., NBC).

Video: search YouTube for "explosive plays NFL explained," "play action shot play explained," and "Cover 1 vs Cover 2 deep ball."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 3: Safeties & coverages)

quiz.q: Which of these counts as an explosive play?
quiz.w: Analysts usually count passes of 20+ yards and runs of 10+ (some use 12+) as explosive.

quiz.q: Why does a play-action fake help a deep throw?
o: Linebackers step forward to stop the run, emptying the space behind them
It makes the pass a run in the stats
It moves the line of scrimmage
quiz.w: The fake pulls run defenders forward (Lesson 16), and the throw goes over them.

quiz.q: 1st-and-10, QB under center, receivers split wide, one safety deep in the middle. Your drill call?
o: PASS: it's the classic shot setup against a 1-high shell
RUN: the quarterback is under center
quiz.w: One deep safety can't cover two deep routes. Teams often take their shot on 1st down with play-action.
